culture.textEn: {ko:가위바위보} (gawibawibo) is rock-paper-scissors. Each player holds out a hand in one of three shapes, and the shapes decide who goes first or who wins.

sources.title: 가위바위보(가위바위褓)
sources.publisher: 국립국어원 (National Institute of Korean Language) — 표준국어대사전
sources.quoteOrLocator: 가위바위보 「명사」 뜻풀이 첫 문장: 손을 내밀어 그 모양에 따라 순서나 승부를 정하는 방법. 둘째 문장은 두 손가락만 편 가위, 주먹을 쥔 바위, 손가락을 모두 편 보와 세 모양 사이의 이기고 지는 관계를 설명함.

sources.title: 가위바위보
sources.quoteOrLocator: 정의: 한 손으로 세 가지 모양을 만들어 차례나 승부를 결정하는 놀이로 풀이함. 내용 단락: 둘 이상이 구호에 맞춰 동시에 손 모양을 내밀고, 같은 모양이 나오면 다시 하며, 늦게 내면 진 것으로 친다는 놀이 방법 설명.

verification.notes:
Line 1 (passes: 1, author sourcing, 2026-10-30): the claim is that 가위바위보 is rock-paper-scissors and that the hand shapes decide who goes first or who wins. The Standard Korean Language Dictionary entry 가위바위보 defines it as holding out a hand and settling order or victory by its shape; the Encyclopedia of Korean Culture entry defines it as a game of three hand shapes that decides turns or victory. Both sources resolved on 2026-10-30. The note is English; the locators are Korean summaries.
Line 2 (passes: 2, independent fact-check, MAR culture and facts checker, a separate session that did not author the cell, 2026-10-30): both URLs reopened; the dictionary's 순서나 승부를 정하는 방법 and the encyclopedia's 차례나 승부를 결정 support the note. Finding: the draft said the hands are shown at the same time, which only the encyclopedia (not on the section 6.6 allowlist) says; the reviser removed it, so the note now says each player holds out a hand in one of three shapes (the dictionary's wording). No origin claim: the game is not framed as Korean in origin (section 5.1).
Line 3 (passes: 3, MAR third pass, an independent session, 2026-10-30): both sources reopened; the revised wording matches the dictionary; no run of words is shared with either locator; no all-Koreans claim, no age wording. Outcome: pass.

culture.textEn: Scissors, {ko:가위} (gawi), beat paper, {ko:보} (bo), the open hand; rock, {ko:바위} (bawi), beats scissors; and paper beats rock.

sources.title: 가위바위보(가위바위褓)
sources.publisher: 국립국어원 (National Institute of Korean Language) — 표준국어대사전
sources.quoteOrLocator: 가위바위보 「명사」 뜻풀이 첫 문장: 손을 내밀어 그 모양에 따라 순서나 승부를 정하는 방법. 둘째 문장은 두 손가락만 편 가위, 주먹을 쥔 바위, 손가락을 모두 편 보와 세 모양 사이의 이기고 지는 관계를 설명함.

sources.title: 가위바위보
sources.quoteOrLocator: 정의: 한 손으로 세 가지 모양을 만들어 차례나 승부를 결정하는 놀이로 풀이함. 내용 단락: 둘 이상이 구호에 맞춰 동시에 손 모양을 내밀고, 같은 모양이 나오면 다시 하며, 늦게 내면 진 것으로 친다는 놀이 방법 설명.

verification.notes:
Line 1 (passes: 1, author sourcing, 2026-10-30): the claim is the win cycle: scissors beat paper (the open hand), rock beats scissors, paper beats rock. The Standard Korean Language Dictionary entry 가위바위보 names the three shapes (two fingers out, a fist, all fingers out) and the cycle; the Encyclopedia of Korean Culture entry gives the same cycle. Both sources resolved on 2026-10-30.
Line 2 (passes: 2, independent fact-check, MAR culture and facts checker, a separate session, 2026-10-30): both URLs reopened; the dictionary's second sentence gives the cycle word for word in Korean; the note's open hand for 보 matches 손가락을 모두 편 것. Outcome: pass.
Line 3 (passes: 3, MAR third pass, an independent session, 2026-10-30): finding: the draft's last sentence (the same hands play again) leaned only on the encyclopedia, which is not on the allowlist; the reviser removed it in en, es and ko. The note now states only the dictionary's cycle; no shared run of words. Outcome: pass with that fix.

culture.textEn: {ko:놀래?} (nollae) and {ko:할래?} (hallae) ask a friend what they want to do. The ending is casual: it has no polite {ko:요} (yo).

sources.title: -ㄹ래
sources.publisher: 국립국어원 (National Institute of Korean Language) — 표준국어대사전
sources.quoteOrLocator: -ㄹ래 「어미」 뜻풀이: 해할 자리에 쓰여 앞으로 하려는 자기 뜻을 나타내거나 상대편의 뜻을 묻는 데 쓰는 종결 어미로 풀이함(요약).

sources.title: 경어(敬語)
sources.quoteOrLocator: 상대경어법 단락: 격식이 필요 없는 가까운 관계에서는 비격식 등급을 쓰고, 이를 해요체(두루높임)와 해체(두루낮춤)로 나누며 해체를 반말로도 부른다는 설명.

verification.notes:
Line 1 (passes: 1, author sourcing, 2026-10-30): the claim is that 놀래? and 할래? ask a friend what they want to do and that the ending is casual, with no polite 요. The Standard Korean Language Dictionary entry -ㄹ래 defines it as a sentence ending of the 해할 (casual) level that states one's own intention or asks the listener's; the Encyclopedia of Korean Culture, 경어, places the 해체 (반말) level in close relationships. Both sources resolved on 2026-10-30.
Line 2 (passes: 2, independent fact-check, MAR culture and facts checker, a separate session, 2026-10-30): both URLs reopened; the dictionary sense covers asking the listener's intention at the casual level; the encyclopedia paragraph covers casual speech between close people. Outcome: pass.
Line 3 (passes: 3, MAR third pass, an independent session, 2026-10-30): both sources reopened; the note matches them and the cell (every -ㄹ래 line is between friends). No shared run of words. Outcome: pass.

culture.textEn: {ko:할게} (halge) says what you will do, like a promise. {ko:내가 먼저 할게!} (naega meonjeo halge) means I'll go first! It is casual, with no {ko:요} (yo).

sources.title: -ㄹ게
sources.publisher: 국립국어원 (National Institute of Korean Language) — 표준국어대사전
sources.quoteOrLocator: -ㄹ게 「어미」 뜻풀이: 구어체로 해할 자리에 쓰여 어떤 행동에 대한 약속이나 의지를 나타내는 종결 어미로 풀이함(요약).

sources.title: 먼저
sources.publisher: 국립국어원 (National Institute of Korean Language) — 표준국어대사전
sources.quoteOrLocator: 먼저 「명사」 뜻풀이: 시간이나 순서에서 앞선 때로 풀이함(요약).

verification.notes:
Line 1 (passes: 1, author sourcing, 2026-10-30): the claim is that 할게 says what you will do, like a promise, that 내가 먼저 할게! means I'll go first, and that it is casual. The Standard Korean Language Dictionary entry -ㄹ게 defines a spoken sentence ending of the 해할 level that states a promise or intention; its entry 먼저 gives the time or order that comes before. Both sources resolved on 2026-10-30.
Line 2 (passes: 2, independent fact-check, MAR culture and facts checker, a separate session, 2026-10-30): both URLs reopened; promise or intention and the casual level are in the -ㄹ게 entry; first in order is in the 먼저 entry. Outcome: pass. The learning design checker asked for halkke; declined: Revised Romanization does not write tensification (F-CNT-002, as 학교 hakgyo), so halge stays.
Line 3 (passes: 3, MAR third pass, an independent session, 2026-10-30): both sources reopened; the note matches them; no shared run of words. Outcome: pass.

notes: Author (MAR, F-CURR-002 section 9.2, 2026-10-30): a content-skill agent wrote the cell from sections 5.1 and 5.6 S4: inviting a friend to play, rock-paper-scissors and who goes first, in three quests with Role Play in each; Practice, Apply and Check triples that differ from Volume 1; two culture and two language notes.

Language checker (independent session, 2026-10-30): casual speech between friends throughout, one polite -yo foil per Role Play turn; romanization is RR of the pronunciation (nollae, hallae, halge, igyeosseo, daeumeun); no heard round asks to tell 내 from 네. One nit: the ko gloss of 이제 read as next time; fixed.

Culture and facts checker (independent session, 2026-10-30): all six source URLs opened; the notes match the NIKL Standard Korean Language Dictionary and the Encyclopedia of Korean Culture; no Korean-origin claim for rock-paper-scissors, no stereotype, brand or real person; one nit: n1 said at the same time, which only the off-allowlist source says; removed.

Learning design checker (independent session, 2026-10-30): the q1 Role Play reply 축구 하자 was asked but never taught (now 줄넘기 하자, Stage 2 Play); the q3 Cloze tile 할래 also completed 내가 먼저 ___ (now 차례야). Declined: halkke for 할게, as RR writes no tensification (F-CNT-002).
Reviser (2026-10-30): applied the findings above to the cell and to its es and ko overlays.

Third pass (independent session, 2026-10-30): confirmed the revisions; n2's same-hands line leaned only on the off-allowlist source (removed); every Tap to Respond turn had two polite -yo distractors, so one per turn is now a casual line of the cell that cannot answer; an es reward line recast. Verdict after fixes: pass.

Machine checks: validate-content and the section 9.3 lint with zero findings; U-1 to U-11, the Role Play graph rules, the review-item freeze. No native-speaker or expert review is claimed: MAR is the multi-agent review.
